quarterly_data.quarter: Eli Lilly press release: U.S. FDA approves Inluriyo (imlunestrant) in combination (09-18-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: The U.S. FDA granted full approval to Inluriyo (imlunestrant), an oral estrogen receptor antagonist, in combination with Verzenio (abemaciclib), a CDK4/6 inhibitor, for adults with ER+, HER2-, ESR1-mutated locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer (detected by an FDA-authorized test) with disease progression following at least one line of endocrine therapy. The approval rests on the Phase 3 EMBER-3 trial in patients with ESR1-mutated MBC (n=159; Inluriyo n=92, Inluriyo plus Verzenio n=67), where the combination doubled median progression-free survival versus Inluriyo alone, 11.1 months versus 5.5 months (HR=0.53 [95% CI, 0.35–0.80]). Most adverse events with the combination were Grade 1-2; permanent discontinuation of Inluriyo alone due to adverse reactions in the combination arm occurred in 1% of patients and of Verzenio alone in 3.4%. It is Inluriyo's second FDA approval in less than a year, after the September 2025 monotherapy approval, and the combination is now available in the United States. Inluriyo is also in the Phase 3 EMBER-4 adjuvant trial in ER+, HER2- early breast cancer, which Lilly calls the largest adjuvant oral SERD trial, with more than 8,000 patients enrolled across 650+ sites in 30+ countries; initial results are anticipated in 2027.
quarterly_data.figure: EMBER-3 ESR1-mutated median PFS 11.1 months versus 5.5 months (HR=0.53); n=159; second FDA approval in less than a year; EMBER-4 more than 8,000 patients, initial results 2027
